patients.summary: Battery recycling plant technician with hypertension and gout who joined in 2019, developed noise-induced hearing loss and then symptomatic occupational lead poisoning in 2022 with slow recovery after removal from exposure, and passed a uric acid ureteral stone in early 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to establish with the practice; his last doctor's office is closing its adult panel. Explained the membership and that insurance is still used for labs and specialists. Booked new patient visit 9/17. Release signed for records from his previous primary care office, faxed today. He takes two prescriptions, a blood pressure pill and one for gout. Will bring bottles.

documents.title: Pre-visit reminder
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Reminder call for new patient visit tomorrow 8:40. Asked him to come fasting for labs and bring medication bottles. Confirmed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46M here to establish. Previous PCP office closing adult panel; records requested.

HTN since ~2014, on lisinopril 10 mg for years, no side effects. Doesn't check at home.
Gout since ~2016, a few flares before allopurinol. On allopurinol 300 mg daily since, no flare in over a year. No colchicine at home.
No surgeries. NKDA.

FH: father with HTN, paternal uncle with gout, mother hypothyroid.
SH: married. Works at a battery recycling plant as a technician, long time in plant work. Quit cigarettes about 5 yrs ago. 2-3 beers a week. Rides his road bike most weekends in season.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: BP 136/86, recheck similar. Well appearing. TMs normal. Neck no thyromegaly. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Joints: no tophi, no synovitis. Ext without edema. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. HTN, near goal on lisinopril 10. Continue. Encouraged home cuff.
2. Gout, quiet on allopurinol 300. Uric acid today.
3. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, uric acid; one-time hep C and HIV, he agrees. Tdap given today. Colon screening is due at 45 now; discussed, he'd rather wait until spring. Flu shot in October.
4. Former smoker, light.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Your recent results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Craig, your labs from last week look good. Kidney and liver tests are normal, blood count normal, sugar normal. Uric acid is 6.8, which is close to where we want it on the allopurinol. Cholesterol is acceptable for now. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
34 pages received by fax from previous primary care. Contents: office notes 2013-2019, med lists, labs.
Summary for chart: HTN started on lisinopril 2014. Gout diagnosed 2016, allopurinol started 2017 after recurrent flares. Annual labs 2016-2019 with normal kidney function and blood counts; uric acid 6.5-7.1 on allopurinol. No colonoscopy on file. Tobacco documented as quit. Allergies: none.
Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. No prior reactions. Tolerated well, VIS provided.

documents.title: Visit change
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Office converting routine in-person visits to video during the state emergency. Pt's 3/24 appt cancelled; rebooked as video 4/7. He has enough of both meds.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, rescheduled from the in-person slot in March.
Plant is still running; he's considered essential and is going in. Wears his PPE.
Bought a home BP cuff after the last visit: readings mostly 130s/80s.
No gout flares. Taking allopurinol and lisinopril daily.
Appears well on video, no distress.
A/P: HTN controlled by home readings, continue lisinopril 10. Gout quiet, continue allopurinol 300. Colonoscopy deferred for now given the pandemic. In-person physical in the fall.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax for 90-day refills of lisinopril 10 mg and allopurinol 300 mg. Last seen 4/2020. Approved per PCP protocol, 1 refill each until the physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
47M for yearly exam.
Interval: fine. Working full shifts. Rode a lot this summer.
Meds: lisinopril 10 daily, allopurinol 300 daily. NKDA.
No gout flares this year.
ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, GI or GU complaints.

Exam: vitals reviewed. NAD. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, nontender. Feet: no tophi, 1st MTPs normal. Skin no concerning lesions. PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- HTN: in range today, continue.
- Gout: continue allopurinol, uric acid with labs.
- CRC screening: now ready, GI referral for colonoscopy.
- Flu shot given.
- BMP, CBC, lipids, uric acid.
Return 1 yr, or 6 months for BP.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Craig, everything from your physical came back in range: kidneys, blood count, cholesterol and uric acid. GI should be calling you to set up the colonoscopy.

documents.title: COVID vaccine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Am I able to get the covid shot yet? I work in a plant with a lot of people.

documents.title: RE: COVID vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Manufacturing workers aren't in the current phase yet; the state is expected to open eligibility to your age group next month. Pharmacies are booking online once it opens. Let us know when you've had it so we can record it.

documents.title: COVID-19 vaccination
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt sent photo of his vaccine card through the portal. Pfizer dose 1 on 3/9/21, dose 2 on 3/30/21, both at a retail pharmacy. Entered into immunization history.

documents.title: Colonoscopy prep
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called with prep questions for 4/20. Reviewed clear liquids the day before, split-dose prep timing, need a driver. He can take lisinopril the morning of with a sip of water. Has a ride arranged.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report (outside GI)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside endoscopy center report, received 4/23/21.
Procedure date 4/20/21. Indication: average-risk screening, age 47. Allergies: NKDA.
Prep: good, adequate for screening.
Scope advanced to the cecum, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. Withdrawal 9 min.
Findings: normal mucosa throughout. Small internal hemorrhoids on retroflexion. No polyps or masses.
Impression: normal screening colonoscopy.
Recommendation: repeat in 10 years.

documents.title: Refill authorization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Lisinopril 10 mg and allopurinol 300 mg 90-day refills approved. Physical 9/28 already booked.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
48 y/o man, yearly visit.
Doing well. Colonoscopy in April normal. Fully vaccinated for COVID in March.
Home BPs 130-138 over low 80s. Gout quiet on allopurinol.
Works at the battery plant, rotating floor duties.
Meds lisinopril 10, allopurinol 300. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Ears normal canals and TMs. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No joint swelling, no tophi. No edema. PHQ-2 negative.

Plan: same meds. CMP, CBC, lipids, uric acid. Flu vaccine today. Booster when eligible. 1 year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from your physical are fine overall. Kidney function and blood count normal, cholesterol about the same as 2019, uric acid in range. See you next year.
